page: Amazon Web Services m9g.xlarge is a general-purpose server instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an ARM64 architecture utilizing an AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 processor. The system is equipped with 4 dedicated physical cores running at 3.3 GHz with one thread per core, supported by 64 KB L1d cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 MB L3 cache. It includes 16.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB per core. This instance does not include local storage or a GPU, and it offers a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier performance in single-core operations, with high scores in Geekbench single-core testing and text processing. Single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression also reach the top decile. Memory performance is strong, with a top-tier Passmark memory score and solid uncached read and write bandwidth. However, multi-core performance and complex computational tasks, such as Passmark CPU encryption and overall CPU scores, fall into the weaker percentiles. Large-model LLM inference is also a notable bottleneck, with poor prompt processing speeds on 7B models.

The m9g.xlarge offers qualitative cost efficiency typical of the Graviton ARM64 architecture, delivering high single-threaded efficiency and memory performance relative to its resource footprint. The primary tradeoffs include the lack of local storage, lower multi-core scaling in intensive workloads, and weak cryptographic performance. This server is appropriate for general-purpose workloads, single-threaded data processing, text processing, static web serving, and lightweight database operations.
